(Phone will ring until picked up. This line is

Northward Trains by US Crews 
1. The Portal train dispatcher will notify train crew 
on arrival at Spiral that they will deliver their train 
on arrival at Portal, which will include the delivery 
track. 
2. The U.S. Crew will call the Minneapolis Border 
Service Group (BSG) and inform them of the 
Train ID, crew members’ names and instructions 
for delivery at Portal. This will serve as the one 
(1) hour notification for the BSG. 
3. When the BSG Transportation Service 
Representative (TSR) calls Canada Customs for 
delivery they will tell the inspector the information 
received from the delivering crew, and secure 
permission for delivery on arrival. 
4. U.S. Crews must ascertain that Customs is in 
position, prior to delivery of their train. 
 
5. After the U.S. crew has delivered the train, they 
will report to BOTH, the Canadian Customs and 
U.S. Customs offices.  ALL CREW MEMBERS 
WILL REPORT.  
6. The train will be released after the U.S. crew 
reports through both customs. 
7. Canadian Customs will call the Minneapolis BSG 
with the release. 
8. The U.S. crew will call BSG when train has been 
delivered. 
 
NOTE: U.S. Crews delivering trains to Canada will 
have to have previously reported to Canadian 
Immigration at least once prior.  All crews must 
comply with ID Requirements. Outbound crews are 
required to confirm with the Minneapolis BSG that 
their train has been released prior to departure. 
Crews can do any work pertaining to the train they 
deliver. 
 
Southward Trains by Canadian Crews 
1. The OM will notify  the train crew on arrival at 
Estevan that they will deliver their train on arrival 
at North Portal. 
2. The Weyburn RTC will g ive the one (1) hour 
advance notice to BSG. 
3. The conductor of the train required to deliver into 
the U.S. must contact Border Services on the 
MARAS radio system (1 -612-904-5934) at the 
North switch, North Portal Yard, advising them of 
their arrival and are to request from BSG 
permission from Canada Customs to exit 
Canada. This will also allow BSG to contact U. S. 
Customs informing them of the train’s arrival and 
requesting them to report to the U. S. Depot and 
for permission to deliver. 
4. Minneapolis BSG will call U.S. Customs 
requesting manning of the VACIS. 
5. U.S. Customs will contact the crew by radio to 
advise to pull down. 
6. Crew will pull down and stop if requested, to 
allow for engine inspection or crew review.  
7. U.S. Crews must ascertain that Customs is in 
position, prior to delivery of their train. 
8. The crew will remain with train until it is released 
by U.S.  Customs. Crew will receive the release 
from U.S. Customs via radio. 
9. The Canadian Crew will do any work pertaining 
to the train they deliver. 
 
Once U.S. Customs releases a South ward train, a 
second release from Minneapolis is NOT required. 
Immediately contact Portal sub dispatcher for track 
authority. If contact is not established within 5 
minutes, call the Director of Train Dispatchers. 
 
NOTE: All crews must carry a passport and driver’s 
license or photo identification in order to cross border. 
When outbound crews are boarding trains to leave 
the yard, crewmember must confirm with the BSG 
that the train is released, prior to departing.  
 
---End---

Additional step when closing the gate against 
MNR traffic:

quadrant) and locking the gate, lift the door on the 
MNR post mounted receptacle box and plug in the 
cable coming from the gate.

one way. 
 
Additional step when opening the gate against 
MNR traffic:

post (Northwest quadrant), lift the door on the MNR 
post mounted receptacle box and unplug the cable 
coming from the gate.

Train Transfer between Crews at the 
International Boundary for Trains Entering the 
US.  
 
Relieved Crew: 
When a conductor and/or locomotive engineer are 
relieved, all GBO, DOB, TGBO, clearances, 
authorities, other written instructions, and all 
necessary information in effect must be: 
(i) Transferred to and known to be understood by 
the relieving employee(s).  
Or 
(ii) When tying up online and not transferring in 
person, handled as instructed by the RTC. If 
documentation is to be left, a list of the items must 
be prepared and signed by the crew member(s) 
going off duty. 
 
Relieving Crew: 
(a) The relieving employee(s) must receive and 
understand all information transferred. 
 
(b) When taking control online and not transferring 
in person , prior to moving, the relieving crew must 
contact the RTC to: 
(i) compare all pertinent information. 
(ii) ensure there are no further restrictions. 
(iii) release OCS once the train is complete by 
MP 64. 
 
(c) In CTC or ABS, if able to ascertain the last signal 
indication for their movement, such indication 
applies, otherwise RESTRICTED speed applies to 
the next signal. 
 
Telephone numbers for Border Crossings 
CONTACT NUMBERS 
 
BSG Winnipeg – 1-204-947-8258 
Customs Border Patrol, Pembina. ND –  
1-701-825-5800 – Extension 5823 
 
Procedures for International Border Crossing 
The Noyes station will be the crew change point for 
both US and Canadian Crews.  
 
The Border Services Group (BSG) in Winnipeg will 
be responsible for all custom related work and the 
required notifications. All paperwork will be left on 
the train. 
 
Westward 
1. Train crews will contact the dispatcher 30 
minutes prior to arrival at Noyes and request 
yarding instructions. 
 
2.  If a train encounters any delays enroute, they 
are to notify the dispatcher of their arrival time at 
Noyes so customs can be notified. 
 
3.  On arrival at Noyes, the crew will note on their 
crew-to-crew report if their train is separated at 
the angle crossing and what time the cut was 
made. 
 
 
4. If the crew knows they will require transportation 
back  to TR Falls, they should contact the 
Assistant Chief Clerk in advance so a cab can 
be at Noyes when they  arrive. 
 
5. If the crew is required to take the train into 
Canada for yarding purposes, you will need to 
contact the BSG to see if the train is clear to 
proceed into Canada. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Eastern Region Timetable 
NOYES LAKES SUBDIVISION  22   July 1, 2024 
 
Eastward 
Train crews will contact the dispatcher one hour 
prior to arrival at Noyes and request yarding 
instructions. 
 
1. Border Service Group (BSG) will contact CBP 
(US Customs) (1 -701-825-5800) with the one 
hour out notice.   CBP will process the train. 
(This will also serve as notification that the CBP 
Rail VACIS team will need to be in position and 
ready the VACIS system within the hour). 
 
2. Once the train is 30 minutes from Emerson the 
crew will contact the RTC. The RTC will contact 
the BSG (1-204-947-8258) and inform them that 
the train is 30 minutes out. The BSG will contact 
CBP to advise them of the pending train and 
have them proceed to the VACIS Booth. Once 
CBP are in position they will radio the crew to 
pull down to the VACIS. 
 
3. Train Crew will proceed up to the Emerson Golf 
Course Crossing and wait for CBP to advise 
okay to proceed to the border.   
 
4. If CP US crew is required to get a train at the 
Golf Course crossing, or out of Emerson Yard, 
they will need to contact the BSG and let them 
know when crew will be going over for the train, 
and the estimated time train is expected to be 
ready to cross the border. If train needs to make 
moves across the border to double train 
together, BSG will get permission from customs 
to do this and pass the information on to the 
crew.   
 
5. If a crew arrives at the crossing and have not 
received the okay to proceed from CBP the crew 
will attempt to contact CBP via Radio on AAR 
Channel 081-081   (All communication with CBP 
will be on the same channel whether Canadian 
or US crew delivering). 
 
6. Crews taking Eastward Trains out of Noyes 
MUST contact the BSG prior to departing, to 
ensure their train has been cleared and there 
are no set outs, unless crew brought the train 
across and were cleared. 
 
Noyes Vehicle Cargo Inspection System  
The Vehicle Cargo Inspection System (VACIS) at 
the Noyes/Emerson border point is fully operational 
and all eastbound trains entering the United States 
will be scanned. 
 
1. When bringing a train into the USA, leave radio 
on AAR channel 081 -081, CBP (Customs & 
Border Patrol) has a radio with that channel. 
 
2. The CBP will inform train crew when the VACIS 
is ready for train to pull down to the VACIS. 
 
3. When advised to proceed the train will proceed 
through the VACIS. Once the cab of the lead 
locomotive is fully through the VACIS, the CBP 
officers will turn the VACIS on and begin 
scanning the train. The VACIS light will be 
engaged when scanning begins. 
 
 
 
 
 
4. While pulling through the VACIS the train crew 
must maintain a speed of between 5 MPH and 
7.5 MPH. If at any time the train is moving too 
quickly the CBP will advise the crew to slow 
down. 
 
5. If at any time the train is proceeding through the 
VACIS and the CBP officer spots an anomaly 
that concerns them, the train crew will be 
contacted and instructed to stop the train. The 
train crew will stop the train as quickly and safely 
as practicable. 
 
6. If car needs to be inspected, the CBP will ask for 
Three Point protection from the crew. CBP will 
not approach the train until CP crew 
acknowledges the Three Point protection to 
CBP.  This will ensure the train will not be 
moved while CBP inspects the car(s). CPB will 
release Three Point protection once clear of 
train. The crew will advise the RTC/Dispatcher 
that they have stopped, and delay incurred. 
 
7. The Customs officer will not be opening cars in 
the train. If they need to have a car opened it will 
have to be set out and it will be looked at 
Monday through Friday from 0700 to 1500 hrs. If 
it is an emergency situation and the car must be 
opened the Barman may be called out but the 
Trainmaster or Roadmaster must also be 
contacted. 
 
8. Once the train has passed fully through the 
VACIS and CBP officers are satisfied that no 
anomalies exist, then the CBP officer will advise 
the train crew that they are cleared through 
customs.  If an anomaly does exist then the train 
crew will be required to comply with the 
instructions from the CBP - VACIS officers. 
 
9. If CBP determines there is a hold car they will 
notify the crew of the car number that they 
require to be set out. CBP will also notify BSG of 
any cars on hold.   
Note: If the VACIS is not operational for any 
reason, trains will not be delayed, but CBP 
personnel will revert to the visual inspection and 
clearance procedures. 
 
Noyes Setting Out Cars for Inspection 
If cars are required to be set out for unloading or 
inspection, they should be set out on the Stock 
track as follows:  
• Boxcar - spotted by the door on the North/West 
side of the building so the door on the car lines 
up with the door on the building. 
• Cars loaded with containers or trailers should 
be spotted to the East/South end of the 
building, where the Top Lifter will be able to get 
to it, using the pad area on this side of the 
building. 
 
Cars set out must be noted on the 125 report. 
 
Noyes Trains Already on US Side of Border 
BSG should be contacted before departure to 
ensure train is OK to move and there are no cars to 
be set out by the inspection warehouse. 
 
---END---

Remote Activated Switches 
Radio Touch Tone power -controlled switches placed 
in service and are identified by signs for the On 
Station (OS) track segment reading BEGIN OS 
TRACK and END OS TRACK. Power Switches will be 
protected by switch point indicator signals. 
 
Shoreham  
• West runner/Superior Connection switch. Green 
 when lined for west runner track and yellow 
 when lined for Superior Connection track.   
Transmit touch tone number #0015 for location 
then  11 for normal or 33 for reverse using radio 
channel (AAR 084-084).  
 
• West runner/BNSF transfer switch to BNSF. Green 
 when lined for west runner and yellow when lined 
 for  BNSF transfer track.  Transmit touch tone 
 number #0015 for location then 11 for normal 
 or 55 for reverse using radio channel  (AAR 084 -
 084).  
US Eastern Region Timetable  
PAYNESVILLE SUBDIVISION  28  July 1, 2024 
 
 
NOTE - The above two locations are incorporated 
together at same location.  Westward movement top 
signal indicator will be for Superior connection switch 
and bottom for BNSF transfer switch.  Eastward 
movement top signal indicator will be of BNSF 
transfer switch and bottom for Superior Connection 
switch. 
 
• Loop/west runner Divide Switch. Green when 
lined for  West runner and yellow when lined for 
Loop track Crew member will transmit touch tone 
number #0010 for location then 11 for normal or 
22 for reverse using radio channel (AAR 084 -
084). 
 
The following will apply to the operation of the power -
controlled switches by radio touch tone: 
 
• Train or engine movement must approach switch 
prepared to stop. 
• Use touch tone number for switch position before 
passing the OS sign location. This must be done 
for each movement over the switch. 
• Switch point indicator will change accordingly 
from green or yellow aspect based upon request. 
• Movement may proceed through the OS section 
once switch is lined and verified for route by 
switch point indicator. 
 
If indicator light displays Red or no indication is 
displayed, stop movement before passing OS sign. 
Switch must then be hand operated per GCOR 9.13.1 
(Hand Operation of Dual Control Switches), 
permission from control operator is not necessary to 
hand operate this switch.   
 
NOTE - Once switch route is requested that route is 
locked, no other requests will be accepted by the 
location until movement is complete through the OS 
segment or after the expiration of 6 minutes in case of 
no movement.  
 
Maintenance of Way movements must hand operate 
the power switch as outlined above for their 
movements and be clear of switch location before 
putting switch back on power. 
 
Remote Activated Derail 
Humboldt - Radio Touch Tone controlled Derail in 
service on Receiver 1 track at Humboldt MP 3.8. 
Derail will be protected by switch point indicator, Red 
for derailing position and Green for non -derailing 
position. 
 
The following will apply to the operation of the Radio -
Controlled Derail by radio touch tone: 
• Train or engine movement must occupy track 
circuit on Receiver 1 which is located between 
Humboldt Ave and 45 th Ave North in order for 
radio touch tone to work.  
• Crew member will transmit touch tone number 
038  using radio channel AAR (094-094) 
• The derail will then move to non -derailing 
position. 
• Derail indicator will change from red aspect to 
 green aspect. 
• Movement may proceed once green aspect is 
 received.  
•  Derail will realign to derailing position once 
movement clears the track circuits between 
Humboldt Ave and 45th Ave North. 
• Once aligned to derailing position red aspect will be 
displayed and location will transmit message  
“CP DERAIL MP 3.8 IN DERAILING POSITION” 
Crew member will confirm derail message with 
Engineer in accordance with GCOR 6.1.1 (Verbal 
Communication). 
• If message is NOT heard after rear of train clears 
45th Ave North or Humboldt Ave within 1 minute. 
Movement will come to stop and crew member will 
hand operate the power switch derail back to 
derailing position in accordance with GCOR 8.20 or 
an understanding has been reached between other 
employees that they will line the power switch derail  
back to derailing position.  When no message is 
received, crew member will report this to the train 
dispatcher who will inform the communication 
center.  
 
If derail indicator light does not display green aspect 
then the power derail must be operated by hand 
before proceeding. Hand operate the derail as 
follows: 
 
• Stop movement before passing indicator for the 
derail, 
• Unlock the switch lock, 
• Place selector lever in hand position, 
• Operate the hand throw lever until derail is seen to 
 move and then line to desired position, 
• Do not return selector lever to the power position 
until at least one unit or car has passed over the 
location of the derail. 
 
When derail is returned to power position and 
movement is clear of the track circuits, the derail will 
automatically return to normal position.   
 
Maintenance of Way must hand operate the power 
derail for their movements as outlined above and 
movement must be clear of location of derail before 
putting back on power.

TrAM Area 
The Merriam Park Sub is TrAM Area 1. 
 
Block System 
Centralized Traffic Control is in use between St. Paul 
Yard and Merriam Park. 
 
Between St. Paul Yard and Hoffman Ave. controlled 
by BNSF East Hump train dispatcher. 
 
Between Hoffman Ave and St. Croix - The following 
will apply to intermediate number plated signals for 
NO 1 and NO 2 MT’s:  Intermediate number plated 
signal displaying a red aspect, train must stop before 
passing the signal and then proceed at restricted 
speed, if signal is equipped with a “G” marker, train 
need not stop but must proceed at restricted speed.  
 
On BNSF trackage between Division Street and St 
Croix, Approach Medium (flashing Yellow) signal 
aspect applies, indication “Proceed prepared to pass 
next signal not exceeding 40 MPH and be prepared to 
enter diverging route at prescribed speed”. 
 
Positive Train Control (PTC)  
PTC is in effect on the Merriam Park Sub. 
 
Movement Authority  
St. Paul Union Depot  
Movements in either direction on Merriam Park Sub 
and UP Spur track between Robert St. and the BNSF 
Hoffman Ave must be coordinated by the CP River/WI 
train dispatcher and the BNSF East Hump train 
dispatcher. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CP train dispatcher controls movement for the Robert 
St. Interlocking including to CP 5305 on the UP -Spur 
Track.  The BNSF East Hump train dispatcher 
controls movements on St Paul Union Depot tracks 1, 
2 and 3 and UP Spud track to 7 th street (west leg of 
Spud wye) and Division St (south leg of Spur wye), 
this includes eastward control signal at MP 530.09 CP 
5301, CP 5304, and CP 5305, BNSF East hump train 
dispatcher radio is AAR 076 call in code 200. 
 
All train movements on St Paul Union Depot tracks 
including UP Spud track to 7 th street and Division St 
on BNSF must obtain a BNSF General Track Bulletin 
(GTB) prior to operating within these limits. 
 
Trains operating from UP Albert Lea Sub and UP 
Roseport industrial lead must contact UP Yardmaster 
at South St. Paul and receive permission before 
passing Junction Switch. If signal does not display a 
proceed indication at Junction Switch, contact the UP-
train dispatcher. 
 
Trains operating to the UP South St. Paul via Hoffman 
Ave. (Belt), or State Street via Union Depot must 
secure permission from UP Yardmaster at South St. 
Paul before passing east end of Hoffman Ave. 
 
Western Ave. – Eastward train and engine 
movements from UP trackage at Western Ave. must 
contact CP River/WI train dispatcher. 
 
Westward train and engine movements from CP 
trackage to Western Ave. must secure permission 
from UP South St. Paul Yardmaster before passing 
Robert Street. Southward movements beyond MP 2.3 
on UP Mankato Subdivision must be authorized by 
UP train dispatcher. (Radio AAR 052-052 *44). 
 
Main Track Designation 
Two main tracks are in use between St. Paul Yard and 
Chestnut St. Beginning at the north, the main tracks 
are numbered NO 1 and NO 2. 
 
Between St. Paul Yard and Hoffman Ave., the main 
tracks are used jointly with the BNSF railroad. 
 
BNSF mileposts apply to NO 2 MT between St. Croix 
and Newport and to NO 1 MT between Newport and 
St. Paul Yard. 
 
CP mileposts apply to NO 1 MT between St. Croix 
and Newport and to NO 2 MT between Newport and 
St. Paul Yard.   
 
CP and BNSF owned tracks will be identified by the 
mile post number followed by the letter “C” for CP 
trackage or the letter “B” for BNSF trackage. 
 
Interlocking/Control Points 
Robert Street – Manual interlocking controlled by CP 
River/Wisconsin train dispatcher. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Eastern Region Timetable 
MERRIAM PARK SUBDIVISON  37  July 1, 2024 
 
Robert Street - When necessary to handle the dual 
control switch in manual operation or to take head 
room into the interlocking, after movement has been 
completed and is clear of the interlocking and 
switches restored to power, crew must actuate the 
push button control located on relay house for the 
affected track, failure to do this will result in a track 
occupancy indication being displayed. No movement 
may be fouling the interlocking at the time the push 
button is actuated. 
 
Equipment Restrictions  
St Paul Yard - Engine(s) must not be parked or 
stored in the following locations at St. Paul Yard: 21 
Pocket, 43 Pocket and east end of 1 Pocket or Mini 
Rip track. 
 
Between Merriam Park and Chestnut St. - 
This area is defined as heavy grade and two -way 
telemetry device is required, as applicable.  
 
Between MP 413 and MP 415 –  
Auto Racks and Double Stack Containers are 
prohibited on the Merriam Park Sub between MP 413 
and MP 415 due to bridge height clearance. 
 
St Paul Union Depot - Due to restricted clearances 
within the Union Depot freight trains are prohibited to 
use track within the depot unless authorization is 
received by the Ramsey County Rail authority. 
 
Movement over Public Crossings 
Chestnut Street - Eastward train movements on 
Merriam Park Sub or off the UP trackage approaching 
Chestnut Street must remain 500 feet back of 
Absolute signals or at location of signs posted until a 
proceed signal governing movement is received to 
make sure traffic pre-emption for vehicle traffic signals 
are working before crossing gates descend. 
 
Continuous Quiet Zone – GCOR 5.8.4 
St. Paul - 
 Market/Ontario St   MP 410.96 
 Chestnut Street   MP 411.13 
 Western Ave   MP 412.08 
 Erie Street   MP 412.38 
 Oneida Street   MP 412.43 
 Carroll Ave   MP 415.51 
 
Movements in St Paul Yard  
St. Paul Yard – Prior to entering St. Paul yard, all 
movements must contact the General Yardmaster for 
yarding instructions and to determine which 
assignments are working within the yard. 
 
Once notified on the assignments that are working, 
each assignment must be contacted to determine that 
there are no conflicting movements on the route to be 
used that was given by the General Yardmaster. 
 
The General Yardmaster must be notified when 
movement starts in on a track at Dunn yard. 
 
 
 
Crews instructed to use tracks in St. Paul Yard other 
than classification tracks, must obtain permission from 
the General Yardmaster prior to entering, leaving, or 
occupying such tracks.  In addition, they must also 
obtain permission from General Yardmaster to make a 
move on any track in Dunn yard.  
 
Movements moving eastward on tracks OB1, OB2,OB 
3 and OB4, will remain clear of the other three tracks 
unless proceed signal is displayed on governing 
absolute signal at Oakland or signal is not needed to 
complete movement.  
 
Movements moving eastward on tracks R1, R2, R3, 
R4, R 5 and R6 will remain clear of the lead on the 
east end  unless a proceed signal is displayed on 
governing absolute signal at Red Rock or signal is not 
needed to complete movement. 
 
St Paul Yard Diesel House  – Diesel House  tracks 
are under the jurisdiction and control of Mechanical 
Department personnel. All movements will comply 
with instructions from the Mechanical Foreman in 
charge. 
 
Movements must not enter Diesel House tracks 
without first obtaining permission from the Diesel 
House Foreman on radio channel 7 (AAR 028 -028), 
or through the General Yardmaster. 
 
Movements departing Diesel House tracks including 
21 pocket need permission from the General 
Yardmaster. 
 
St Paul Yard Rip Tracks - Movements on Rip Tracks 
moving in either direction on the old eastbound track 
must ring the engine bell continuously sufficiently in 
advance approaching and passing cars on Rip 1 to 
provide warning to employees.  
 
St. Paul Yard Roundhouse crossing - White 
indication lights are installed on  a line pole just west 
of roundhouse crossing for outbound trains to indicate 
when Hoffman Ave. shows an indication to proceed.  
If white light is not displayed outbound trains will 
remain behind roundhouse crossing until either 
authorized by control operator to proceed or white 
light is displayed. 
 
St. Paul Yard - Shove Lights 
The General Yardmaster is in charge of tracks under 
shove light protection. Shove lights are located on the 
West end of tracks 1, 2, 3, 4, tracks 42, 43, 44, 45, 46 
and 47 and East end of tracks R1, R2, R3, R4, R5 
and R6 in Dunn Yard. These lights indicate the 
number of car lengths of room remaining at the 
opposite end of the track. Before cars are shoved into 
these tracks using shove lights, a job briefing between 
crew member and General Yardmaster must be made 
to determine track is clear for the movement per 
GCOR Rule 6.5.  Crew members will job brief on the 
move to be made using shove lights. During this 
movement no other unrelated task outside of this 
move may be made. 
  
 
US Eastern Region Timetable 
MERRIAM PARK SUBDIVISON  38  July 1, 2024 
 
How the lights work : When cars are shoved into 
tracks the leading pair of wheels on the leading car 
will shunt each circuit in order of the 4 vertical lights , 
and each light will be extinguished as the leading 
wheel shunts each circuit. 
Single engine, engine consists, or cars must not be 
left standing within the shove light circuits unless such 
equipment is coupled to and part of a train, transfer or 
cut of cars occupying the track protected by the shove 
indicators. 
 
When various circuits are not occupied, the lights in 
the indicator will be illuminated. 
 
Indications displayed:  
  3= 12 car lengths approximately 600 feet 
 2 = 8 car lengths approximately 400 feet 
 1= 4 car lengths approximately 200 feet 
 0 = STOP Track is Full  
 
Shove light status will be communicated at a 
minimum of 20 - 30 car intervals while shoving into 
the track until the top light of the four lights is 
extinguished.   
 
Example: Prior to making a shove move using the 
shove lights, a member of the crew must ascertain the 
track is clear from the Yardmaster. Once it is known 
that the track is clear, the Conductor will state the 
following: 
“CP 8510, we have all of the shove lights, OK to 
shove (East or West)” 
 
Once 20 – 30 cars pass by the Conductor will state: 
 “CP 8510 we still have all the lights.”  
 
This will continue until the first light extinguishes, then 
the Conductor will state: 
 “CP 8510, 3 lights to a Stop”  
 “CP 8510, 2 lights to a Stop” 
 “CP 8510, 1 light to a Stop” 
 “CP 8510, Stop the track is full.” 
 
Each subsequent light will be communicated and 
responded to by the Engineer as movements are to 
be consistent with good train handling. The cut must 
be stopped when the all the lights are extinguished.  
The track will then be considered full with no further 
shove movements into the circuit permitted. 
 
Red Rock Industrial Lead - Movements must 
receive permission from General Yardmaster to enter 
Red Rock industrial lead track. 
 
Trains, engines, or cars must not be left on the Red 
Rock industrial lead without permission from the 
General Yardmaster. 
 
Normal position of hand operated switches located on 
the Red Rock industrial lead will be lined and locked 
for the industrial lead. 
 
St Paul Yard - Hump and Classification Yard 
Instructions  
Duties of the General Yardmaster 
The General Yardmaster will also supervise hump 
switch crews, and car department personnel working 
under their jurisdiction. 
 
Classification Yard Instructions 
Engineer in charge of engine humping must comply 
with instructions received, except in cases of 
emergency.  When shoving cars from Dunn and up to 
the crest of the hump, a crew member or other 
qualified employee must ride leading car or walk 
ahead of movement to ascertain switches are 
properly lined.  
 
Crew must know that cars are coupled, before moving 
cars over hump. Hump Foremen must instruct their 
crews in this respect and know that instructions are 
complied with.  
 
Hump Procedures/Restrictions 
Yardmasters must monitor the “Pro -Yards” automatic 
hump system to assure that cars are moving over the 
hump at proper speed. 
  
Cabooses must not be released over the hump. 
Cabooses must not be used during humping 
operation and must be shoved to rest or handled by 
themselves. 
 
Do not move empty or loaded deep well intermodal 
cars (depressed flats or double stack/triple stack) and 
empty or loaded depressed center beam lumber cars 
in series CP 320000 through CP 320029 through the 
hump retarders. 
 
When cars are found bad order or made bad order 
and not marked bad order on switch list, Hump 
Foremen must call attention to such cars and get 
disposition from Yardmaster. Yardmaster must contact 
mechanical forces to have car Bad Ordered in TYES. 
 
St Paul Yard - Restricted clearance exists between 
tracks 7 and 8. When cars are located on either or 
both tracks’ employees must not ride the side of car 
between tracks 7 and 8. 
 
Manual Operation of Air Switches in the Hump 
Yard  
The following guidelines will be used when using air 
switches in manual operation: 
1. Request a block for protection from the 
Yardmaster on radio channel AAR 41-41 
2. Assure switches are lined away from the 
affected working limits. 
3. Remove the air from the switch. 
4. Apply a switch point clamp and tag the 
switch out of service. 
5. Lock the switch with an effective locking 
device. (OTS rule 21.2.1) 
Contact S&C Manager before any work begins.  
 
 
 
 
US Eastern Region Timetable 
MERRIAM PARK SUBDIVISON  39  July 1, 2024 
 
Classification tracks  
West End CT04 through CT41 
Classification (bowl) tracks CT0 4 through CT41 are 
protected on the west end by a system of inert 
retarders and track skates.  These tracks do not 
require hand brakes unless otherwise instructed. 
 
Track skates will be placed west of inert retarders and 
sufficiently east of fouling point for track used.  Sand 
is located between the rail at the west end of each 
track in the bowl.  Before applying skates to any of 
these tracks (15 feet west of the inert retarders) place 
2 feet of san d on top of the rail with skate.  Place 
skates in the middle of the 2 feet of sand.  Do not 
stagger or off set skates but make sure they are 
directly across from each other on the track.    
 
Track skates will be removed only when engines are 
entering those tracks to pull or switch cars.  After 
crews are finished with the use of track(s), skates 
must be replaced on the track(s) by the crew who 
removed them before the block is released to the 
General Yardmaster. 
 
Humping to a Clear Track 
The following instructions govern humping into clear 
tracks: 
 1.  When the General Yardmaster is advised that a 
classification track is clear, the General 
Yardmaster will put a “peg” on the track. 
 
 2. General Yardmaster will announce on radio 
channel 5 (AAR 088 -088) when car is going up a 
clear track and use the “Pack a Track” or “Stall” 
feature to reduce the speed of cars going into an 
open alley. 
 
Over-speed Alarm 
Whenever the “over speed alarm” is tripped during 
humping operations the “contaminated wheel 
process” must be completed before humping is 
resumed. The first three cars that are humped after an 
over speed must not go to a clear track. 
 
Movement from Hump into Bowl 
If necessary for hump engine to move into 
classification yard, ground crew must accompany 
engine. Engine must not be moved through retarders 
in either direction when retarders are in closed 
position.   
 
Cars must not be pulled or shoved through retarders 
when retarders are in closed position without 
permission from the proper authority. 
 
Shoving Tracks from Hump End 
The hump crew must notify the General Yardmaster 
when a track is to be shoved and General yardmaster 
will arrange for protection of the shove.  Hump crew 
will inform General Yardmaster when shove move is 
completed. 
 
 
 
 
 
Placement of Cars West End of Bowl Tracks 
When cars are pulled out of the bowl from the hump 
end of the yard and cars are left on the track, 
remaining cars must be left no farther west than the 
inerts. 
 
When cars are added to the west end of the bowl 
tracks, they must be placed at least into the inert 
retarder. If cars are on the track and extend west of 
the inert, the added car(s) must be coupled to them. 
 
Requesting and Releasing Blocks on Bowl Tracks 
Any time a train crew or other craft needs to enter a 
track in the hump classification yard those employees 
must contact the General Yardmaster when on duty 
and request a block on the track or tracks. 
 
General Yardmaster will block track and notify 
requesting employee that required protection has 
been provided by stating “(Employee or Engine No.) 
has a block on track  (No.).” Requesting employee 
must repeat this information back to General 
Yardmaster. Before commencing any duties on that 
track other protection used by other crafts must be 
established. When work is completed and protection 
is no longer required, employee will notify General 
Yardmaster that block may be released. General 
Yardmaster must keep records on tracks blocked and 
released on the prescribed form with time given 
unless electronically recorded with that information. 
 
After a crew has requested a block on a bowl track 
but has been advised that cars are still “rolling” into 
the track, the crew will wait a minimum of FIVE (5) 
MINUTES before coupling onto the track, unless it 
can be VISUALLY VERIFIED by a member of the 
crew requesting the block that the “rolling” cars have 
coupled to the track.  If a problem is found with 
equipment or track, they have the block on, 
employees must leave protection established in place 
until the situation is remedied, or other protection is 
provided by another craft or employee. 
 
The block may be released when the engine moves 
off the classification track. A block is also required 
when an engine is parked on the west end of a 
classification track when a crew goes to lunch or is 
tying up. The block is to be released when the crew is 
clear of the classification tracks. Likewise, a crew 
coming out of lunch must request a block before 
taking charge of their engine parked on a 
classification track. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Eastern Region Timetable 
MERRIAM PARK SUBDIVISON  40  July 1, 2024 
 
Drill Signals Red Rock and Dunn 
When the signal at Red Rock from the Industrial Lead 
to the Industrial Lead or at Dunn from the Yard to the 
Industrial Lead or Industrial Lead into the Yard is 
needed multiple times for switching moves, after 
contacting the St. Paul Yardmaster for permission on 
the Industrial Lead, you may contact the BNSF East 
Hump Dispatcher and request the signal to be placed 
in what is known as “Drill”. When the signal is in “Drill” 
it will continually display a Flashing Red/Red 
indication. This indication will remain even when the 
limits between the signals is occupied. This is how the 
system is designed and is not malfunctioning so while 
you are switching at this location, you will constantly 
have the signal. Once you are finished using the 
“Drill” you will then contact the BNSF East Hump 
Dispatcher and release it back to them. 
 
St Paul Yard - Remote Control Locomotives 
Remote Control Operations may be in use between 
Red Rock and Hoffman Ave. Locomotive cab may not 
be occupied. 
 
Prior making any movements within St. Paul Yard that 
will be in a location that has remote control zones, all 
movements must contact the St. Paul Yardmaster to 
determine if there are any of the remote -control zones 
activated. Engineering employees that have work to  
perform in the area of the remote -control zones also 
have to determine if any zones are active. 
 
No Zones Active: 
The inbound train, outbound train, lite engine, or other 
assignment will receive yarding, departing or 
movement instructions and if there are no zones 
activated, the movement will then follow the 
instructions that are given by the Yardmaster.  
 
Active Zone: 
After receiving instruction from the Yardmaster and 
there is an active zone or zones and the inbound 
train, outbound train, lite engine, or other assignment 
will come into contact with an active zone, the 
movement must contact the Remote-Control Operator 
(RCO) to be granted access into that remote control 
zone and follow any instructions given by the RCO. 
The Conductor on the inbound or outbound train will 
also document on the Delay Report the time that they 
entered the Remote -Control Zone and the time that 
they cleared the Remote-Control Zone. 
 
Once the movement is clear of the remote -control 
zone the RCO must be advised, and the position of 
any switches used within the zone. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The Remote-Control Zones are as follows:  
The zones will begin on the east end of Dunn Yard at 
the clearance point of the switch and each track will 
be its own individual zone as follows: 
R1 = Zone 1   
R2 = Zone 2 
R3 = Zone 3 
R4 = Zone 4 
R5 = Zone 5 
R6 = Zone 6 
 
The zones on the west end will include the track from 
the switch of that specific zone, up the hump lead and 
end at the crest of the hump. 
 
General Information 
Heavy Grade 
MP 416.0 – MP 410.0 EWD Avg. Grade 1.30%

General Information 
Drill Signals Red Rock and Dunn 
When the signal at Red Rock from the Industrial 
Lead to the Industrial Lead or at Dunn from the Yard 
to the Industrial Lead or Industrial Lead into the 
Yard is needed multiple times for switching moves, 
after contacting the St. Paul Yardmaster for 
permission on the Industrial Lead, you may contact 
the BNSF East Hump Dispatcher and request the 
signal to be placed in what is known as “Drill”. 
When the signal is in “Drill” it will continually display 
a Flashing Red/Red indication. This indication will 
remain even when the limits between the signals is 
occupied. This is how the system is designed and is 
not malfunctioning so while you are switching at this 
location, you will constantly have the signal. Once 
you are finished using the “Drill” you will then 
contact the BNSF East Hump Dispatcher and 
release it back to them. 
 
Eastward Trains Departing St Paul Yard - 
Eastward trains departing St Paul Yard destined for 
River Sub shall notify the River/WI Train Dispatcher 
of their train consist and lead unit after departing St 
Paul Yard between Cottage Grove and St Croix, but 
before entering CP trackage at St. Croix. 
 
 
Colvill - The Colvill West Power derail is field auto -
restoring, when a train move is complete and the 
track goes unoccupied, the derail will automatically 
return to the derailing position. Switch blocks when 
applied by the Dispatcher will override the auto -
restoring feature. 
 
Minnesota City – Westward trains destined for 
Waseca Sub that are going to be left unattended 
must remain east of MP 6.2 on the Waseca Sub.

Track Bulletins 
In compliance with GCOR 15.1 
CP trains operating between Bryn Mawr and Shermer 
must obtain UP track warrant and Eastward trains 
must verify with the UP –train dispatcher if UP track 
bulletins are current before passing Rondout. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Daily Operating Bulletin (DOB) – Metra  
On Elgin, C&M, and Fox Lake Subs, delivery of Track 
Bulletin information is now accomplished in the format 
of a Non –Train Specific Daily Operating Bulletin or 
DOB.   Daily Operating Bulletins are effective at 12:01 
AM each day and remain in effect until cancelled by 
the train dispatcher.  Primary restrictions such as 
Form Bs (B) and Temporary Speed Restrictions (TSR) 
are organized by Subdivision and listed in ascending 
Milepost order on the DOB.  DOBs can be identified 
by a 6 –digit DOB Number, the title “Operating 
Bulletin”, and the date and time issued at the top of 
the first page.  Crews for all movements, including 
Yard moves between CUS and Western Avenue 
Coach Yard, must have a copy of the current DOB.  
Additions or changes to the original DOB may be 
relayed verbally to trains from the Train Dispatcher, or 
updated DOB with a new identifying number may be 
issued.  
 
Metra trains that receive a radio bulletin enroute will 
retain that radio bulletin for return trip. Crews must 
verify with train dispatcher if radio bulletin is still in 
effect prior to the restriction listed.

and Milwaukee, between Tower A 20 and Shermer 
and between Bryn Mawr and Tower B17 under the

between Milwaukee and Cut Off.

occupy a main track without proper signal indication 
or verbal authority from the Wisconsin or C&M train 
dispatcher. Trains will be governed by Track Permit 
GCOR 9.15 when territory is jointly occupied by men 
and/or equipment. Maintenance of Way movements 
will be governed by Track Permit GCOR 9.15. 
 
Between CP Canal and Tower A –2 – Metra North 
Joint Tracks Special Instructions will be in effect and 
employees must provide themselves with a copy 
whose duties require them to use these tracks. 
 
Waxdale Spur – GCOR 6.28 applies.

Unless otherwise specified, the following instructions 
will apply to the Dual Control Switch Point Derails that 
are in service at Milwaukee (Cut Off, North lead) and 
Milwaukee (Grand Ave, North Milwaukee Spur).  
• When the main track switch is locked in normal

yellow and aspect 9.1.10 red over red over green will 
be for 25 MPH crossovers and turnouts east of CN 
Crossing onto the CN Main Track. Signal aspect 9.1.9 
red over yellow over red and aspect 9.1.10 red over 
green over red will be for 40 MPH crossovers just

Franklin Park West. NO 3 MT begins and ends at the 
West Absolute signal for Franklin Park West.  Four 
Main tracks are in use between Tower B12 and 
Franklin Park West.  
 
Two main tracks are in use between Tower B12 and 
Randall Road. Beginning at the north, the main tracks

Schaumburg Industrial Park  
Not more than 25 loads at one time may be shoved 
around 14–degree curve over Irving Park Road. 
 
Six axle locomotives are not permitted on Industrial 
Park tracks, Olympia steel, Nexus, old Nexus and 
Jorgensen Steel tracks.    
 
Six axle GE AC 4400 and EMD SD90MAC

• Schaumburg Industrial Park 
• Itasca Industrial Park 
• Bensenville Industrial Park 
• Bensenville North and South Industries

Within Bensenville yard when handling rail cars 89 
feet or longer or mult i–platform cars, no more than 12

shoving, or doubling power.

Elmwood Park, River Grove, Mannheim, Franklin

Roselle, Hanover Park, Bartlett, National Street, Elgin,

State of Illinois 
Engine whistle must be sounded, regardless of city or 
village ordinances, when a train or engine is meeting 
or passing another train which is stopping, standing, 
or starting from a station platform and when meeting 
or passing another train or engine in the vicinity of a 
grade crossing. In such cases whistle must be 
sounded until the other train or engine has been 
completely passed. 
 
City of Chicago 
The City of Chicago Office of Emergency 
Communications (911) Center has identified the 
following street crossings as being critical emergency 
routes: 
• Harlem Avenue 
• Narragansett Avenue 
• Oak Park Avenue 
When trains are stopped or anticipate being 
obstructing any of these crossings for more than 10 
minutes, a crew member must notify the train 
dispatcher immediately indicating amount of time the 
crossings may be blocked for.  Crew must also notify 
the train dispatcher when the train is clear of the 
crossing.

this crossing operate in conjunction with Absolute 
Signals at Tower B17.   When EWD trains are given 
verbal permission past Absolute Signal displaying

Devices will not activate until head end of movement 
has passed signal.  Rule 6.32.2 applies. 
 
Wood Dale

the crossing warning devices activated on Wood Dale 
and Irving Park Roads. 
 
Spaulding – Train and engine movements on other 
than main track, must stop before occupying 
Spaulding Road crossing and provide warning by 
crew member on ground until crossing is occupied.

Clear man” indicate the same as “No Clearance”.

Metra Director Operations has jurisdiction over all 
METRA passenger train service, including METRA 
Control Operators  
 
METRA passenger trains will be governed by CP 
Rules, Timetable and General Orders. 
 
Schedules of METRA trains operating on the Elgin 
Subdivision are indicated in the METRA commuter 
operations train schedules. 
 
Employees concerned or whose duties are affected 
by the movement of these must provide themselves 
with a copy.  
 
METRA trains must not depart stations before time 
shown in current METRA commuter operations train 
schedules. 
 
Schiller Park Yard   
Tracks 1, 2, 8, 9 and 6 lead are back in service in 
Schiller Park Yard. The rest of the yard remains out of 
service. 
 
Unattended locomotives must be locked account this 
yard does not have 24/7 visibility. 
 
Bensenville Yard  
Prior to entering Bensenville yard, all movements 
must contact the General Yardmaster for yarding 
instructions and to determine which assignments are 
working within the yard. 
 
Once notified on the assignments that are working, 
each assignment must be contacted to determine that 
there are no conflicting movements on the route to be 
used that was given by the General Yardmaster. 
 
Arriving trains must be prepared to give the General 
Yardmaster all necessary information concerning your 
train. 
 
Trains or engines shall advise the General 
Yardmaster before entering the Outbound track at the 
connection hand throw switch and also when clear of 
the connection switch when entering the yard.

Remote Control Operations: 
Remote Control Operation may be in use between 
MP13.6 and MP17 in Bensenville Yard. Locomotive 
cab may not be occupied.

Prior to entering a remote –control area, you must first 
contact the General Yardmaster on radio channel 
088–088 to determine if any remote –control zones 
are active. The General Yardmaster would tell you for 
example that Zone One is active and give assignment 
RCCL1 a call on channel 084 –084 to get permission 
in that zone  
(GCOR 6.7 Item A). 
 
Activation of a Remote–Control Zone: 
Prior to using a remote –control zone, the Remote –
Control Operator will contact the Yardmaster to 
activate the remote –control zone. Once activated the 
Yardmaster will log the activation time in the remote –
control logbook and the Remote–Control Operator will 
verify all switches within that zone are lined for 
Remote Control Operator’s movement. 
 
Zone 1 – D&F Yard 
Outbound track, between the outbound/hump 
pullback divide switch and the west end of the F –yard 
lead (switches 1–21).  Contact crew on Ch. 034–034 
 
Zone 2 – C Yard 
Hump pullback Lead, between the outbound/hump 
pullback divide switch and the west end of the C –yard 
lead (switches 1–25).  Contact crew on Ch. 084–084

New 'Track 0' connecting Control Point Tower A5 MP 
5.4 and Control Point Tower A6 MP 5.7 (631 feet).  
Use of Track Signal indication or Verbal Authority from 
A5 Control Operator CCF.  New Hand throw switch to 
new Southeast Wye Track (300 feet) must be lined 
and locked for Track 0 when not in immediate use.

 Yard must not be blocked by switch crews.

and ambulance service monitor the CP’s radio

work, contact the Saratoga Yardmaster AAR Channel

Saratoga Springs - If any trains need to use the  
Saratoga Springs station tracks  they will need to get 
permission from Saratoga Springs Yardmaster before 
using the tracks. 
 
Saratoga Springs – Prior to accepting a signal at 
CPC36 or CPC35 to enter the yard or performing 
work, contact the Saratoga Yardmaster AAR Channel 
032-032. 
 
Saratoga Yard - Before flat switching cars into any 
tracks in Saratoga yard, crew member(s) must ensure 
that each track that is being switched into is secured 
on at least one end. 
 
No more than 4 loaded cars are allowed to be cut -off 
in motion at a time. 
 
Cars must not be kicked or released to move under 
their own momentum unless the cars being coupled to 
are more than 500 feet (10 car lengths) away. 
 
It is prohibited to release CP 220 series boxcars 
under their own motion. 
 
It is prohibited to release cars under their own motion 
into clear tracks. 
 
Ballston Spa – A “Hold Trains Here” sign has been 
installed for southward trains that are staging on the 
siding at Ballston Spa, 7300 feet south of CPC 33. 
Length permitting, trains must not pass this sign – Do 
not stop locomotives in front of the old passenger 
station north of the sign.  Northward trains must stop 
and hold back at the sign for CPC 33 if stopping or 
staging your train. 
 
Rouses Point Delivery Track 
Extending northward a distance of 1.5 miles between 
CPC 191 and Rouses Point Junction , USA/Canada 
Border Junction with LaColle Sub. Requires 
permission from CP Train Dispatcher. 
 
Northward - Movements may pass CPC 191 after 
receiving either a signal indication or verbal 
permission from CP Train Dispatcher. Northward 
movements must be reported clear at Rouses Point 
Jct to CP Train Dispatcher. 
 
Southward - Movements must not proceed beyond 
Rouses Point Jct MP 0.0 LaColle Sub (USA/Canada 
Border) until verbal authorization is received from the 
CP Train Dispatcher.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
US Eastern Region Timetable  
CANADIAN SUBDIVISON  107  July 1, 2024 
 
Procedures for International Border  
Southward movements on the LaColle Sub must 
STOP their train at LaColle and contact the LaColle 
Sub RTC who will contact Border Services to 
determine whether or not the train has been cleared 
into the U.S. Once Border Services advises the 
LaColle Sub RTC of the final plan, this information will 
be conveyed to the train crew and the train may 
proceed to the border. This authority only allows the 
train to proceed to the border. The train crew must still 
receive permission on the Rouses Point Delivery 
Track from the CP Train Dispatcher and must still 
STOP and receive permission from Border Services 
to pass through the VACIS location. Under no 
circumstances is a crew allowed to pass the VACIS 
location until they have been cleared by Border 
Services. 
 
All southward trains on the Rouses Point Delivery 
Track are required to stop 300 feet north of the VACIS 
inspection location to ensure the speed requirement 
of 5 to 7 mph when passing through the VACIS is met. 
A reflective sign stating “300 ft to VACIS” is placed at 
the required stopping point. Trains being scanned at 
the VACIS must maintain a speed of 5 to 7 mph for 
the entire length of the scan. 
All crews (US & Canadian) are to pull down to the 300 
ft sign and initiate contact with Border Services via 
radio. Crews are required to stay in the cab of the 
locomotive at all times and are not permitted to leave 
the cab of the locomotive to walk between trailing 
locomotives, detrain, or to enter the Rouses Point 
yard office. Trains are not permitted to travel through 
the VACIS until permission is received from Border 
Services. All crew members must present their CP ID 
as well as a personal ID with a picture (Enhanced 
Driver’s License or Passport) to the Border Services 
Officer upon request. If crew change is done prior to 
the VACIS machine, the inbound crew must wait until 
the Border Services Officer arrives and clears the 
crew to depart. 
 
Northward movements from CPC 191 will contact the 
CP Train Dispatcher who will contact Border Services 
to determine whether or not the train has been 
cleared by Border Services or will need to be scanned 
at the VACIS. Once Border Services advises the CP 
Train Dispatcher of the final plan, this information will 
be conveyed to the train crew. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Setting Off or Lifting Custom Hold Cars - Crews 
(US/Canadian) pulling through the VACIS are 
responsible for the following items. 
1. When advised by customs that a Custom hold 
car or multiple cars are to be set off, call the CP  
Dispatcher on the proper radio channel, and 
advise them of the car number(s) to be set off 
and location in the train. CP Train Dispatcher will 
inform the train crew if a custom hold car has 
been released and needs to be lifted. 
2. Make the set off /pick up on the proper track. 
3. Update paperwork to indicating car numbers 
and revise train tonnage, length etc. 
 
It is important to note, unless outlawed, the crew 
pulling though the VACIS is responsible to make the 
set off. 
 
Train crew must not leave Rouses Point until they 
have received permission from one of the following: 
US Customs, CP North Dispatcher or LaColle Sub 
RTC regarding customs clearance. 
 
 
---END---
